question: to the Commission Barbara Bonte (PfE) Subject:

The Commission presents the Global Gateway as a geopolitical instrument designed to strengthen the Union’s strategic autonomy through, among other things, investment in energy corridors, digital connectivity and critical raw materials supply chains. The European Court of Auditors has criticised shortcomings in the reporting, transparency and evaluation of the EFSD+ funding instruments and the External Action Guarantee. 1.

Can the Commission quantify, using aggregate figures, the total amount of private investment that has actually been mobilised since the launch of the Global Gateway in 2021 with the support of EU instruments, in particular the External Action Guarantee and the EFSD+?
What quantifiable benefits for the European Union have been observed since the launch of the Global Gateway?
What measures has the Commission taken to improve reporting, transparency and evaluation of the EFSD+ and the External Action Guarantee?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (13.7.2026) The Commission reports on Global Gateway1 (GG) in terms of total investments mobilised as a result of EU support. Latest joint reporting for 2021–2024 indicates around EUR 306 billion in GG investments2, including operations leveraging private capital alongside public and multilateral resources3. The strategy is yielding economic, geopolitical and strategic benefits for the EU. A broad pipeline of projects has been launched across partner regions, including over 250 flagship projects4 strengthening digital and transport connectivity, energy/raw material supply chains, education, and health security, while improving access for EU businesses to global markets. GG also creates opportunities for EU businesses through the GG Investment Hub5, calls for expressions of interests6, business fora7 or investment packages, encompassing hundreds of sustainable and quality investment projects that, in close cooperation with their partners, the EU and its Member States develop and invest in8. On reporting and transparency, the Commission provides information on the European Fund for Sustainable Development Plus (EFSD+) and the External Action Guarantee in the EU’s yearly draft general budget, notably Working Document Part X on financial instruments and Part XI on budgetary guarantees9 (in the context of the Article 41(5) of the Financial Regulation10). Further information on the EFSD+ and EU budgetary guarantees is available in the 2025 annual report on the implementation of the EU’s external action instruments in 202411. The Commission also provides an overview of all the signed EFSD and EFSD+ guarantee agreements12. Furthermore, in line with Article 33(5) of the Neighbourhood, Development and International Cooperation Instrument–Global Europe (NDICI-GE) Regulation13, agendas and minutes of all EFSD+ Strategic Board meetings are public14.
